outcomes.text: Read the DET–NOM split and distinguish empty DET from a plain pronoun or name.
Locate pre-determiners and trace the layers created by modifiers.
Use meaning to decide where a modifier attaches in a nominal or with an indefinite pronoun.

opening.prompt: Which word names the kind of thing referred to in “those baskets”?

options.feedback: “Those” helps identify which things are meant.
“Baskets” names the things and heads the phrase.
The phrase refers to baskets, and “those” points them out.

opening.prompt: Which phrase puts a word before the determiner “the”?

options.feedback: “Both” comes before the article.
“Blue” follows the article.
The location follows the noun.

opening.prompt: What does “red” describe in “a new red kite”?

options.feedback: “A” is the article.
“New” and “red” describe different properties.
“Red” describes the colour of the kite.

opening.prompt: In “the wooden crates from Cebu”, which group gives the origin?

options.feedback: This group names and describes the crates.
“From Cebu” tells where the crates came from.
This adjective describes what the crates are made of.

opening.prompt: Which complete group does “someone” form in “Someone waved”?

options.feedback: “Someone” is a pronoun that forms the whole subject NP.
“Waved” supplies the verb.
The subject contains a pronoun and has no preposition.

closing.prompt: What does the DET branch contain in “lanterns” in “Lanterns glowed”?

options.feedback: The bare plural has an empty DET. Supplying “the” changes its interpretation.
“Lanterns” is the head noun under NOM.
The bare plural NP has an empty DET branch and an overt NOM.

closing.prompt: In “both these notebooks”, what is the sister of PRE-DET?

options.feedback: “These” stays inside the smaller NP.
“Both” combines with the complete inner NP.
The noun stays inside NOM.

closing.prompt: Read “a small blue lantern” as a blue lantern that is small. Which words form the smaller NOM?

options.feedback: “Small” modifies the group already formed by “blue” and “lantern”.
These words exclude the head noun.
That is the entire NP, including DET.

closing.prompt: In “the metal boxes from Iloilo”, assume “metal boxes” names the kind of box. What does “from Iloilo” attach beside?

options.feedback: The origin belongs with the nominal and leaves DET outside.
The origin applies to the boxes, with “metal” identifying the kind.
The PP adds origin to the group that names the kind of box.

closing.prompt: How is “anyone near the entrance” structured in this analysis?

options.text: A determiner and a noun under NOM
options.feedback: “Anyone” is a pronoun here.

options.text: Pronoun and PP as sisters under NP
options.feedback: “Near the entrance” modifies the indefinite pronoun directly under NP.
“Near” is the head of the PP.
